μέντοι ὁ Σωτὴρ βέλος ἐκλεκτὸν, καὶ ἀνάλογα τῷ Σωτῆρι βέλη τοῦ Θεοῦ οἱ ἅγιοι
τιτρώσκοντες βέ λει ἐκλεκτῷ, ἵνα ὁ τετρωμένος λέγω· Τετρωμένη ἀ γάπης ἐγώ·
οὕτως ὁ Ἀντίχριστος βέλος τοῦ πονη ροῦ. Καὶ πάντες οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ βέλη τοῦ
διαβόλου, οἷς 17.129 κατὰ τῶν δικαίων χρᾶται. Ἴδε γυναῖκα, καὶ ἐπ εβούλευσάν σοι.
Εἰ μὴ βέλος ἐστὶ πεπυρωμένον, πῦρ ἔχουσα ἐν στόματι, ἵνα λαλήσῃ καὶ καύσῃ σε, ἐν
χει ρὶ, ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ σώματι, ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ; Καὶ ὥσπερ ὁ Θεὸς τίθησι τόξον ἐν τῇ
νεφέλῃ, ἵνα παύσῃ χειμῶνα, καὶ μὴ γίνηται κατακλυσμός· οὕτω, κατὰ τὸ
ἀντικείμενον, ὁ πονηρὸς χρᾶται τόξῳ, ἵνα παύσῃ γαλήνην ἀπὸ ψυχῆς, καὶ εἰρήνην
σβέσῃ, καὶ πόλε μον ἐγείρῃ, καὶ χειμῶνα ποιήσῃ. Μήποτε δὲ οἱ πτω χοὶ καὶ πένητες
ἀδελφοί εἰσι τῶν εὐθέων τῇ καρ δίᾳ, οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι, οὓς ζητοῦσι καταβα
λεῖν οἱ δαίμονες. Ἐὰν ἴδῃς σκανδαλιζόμενον, καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας κεκρατημένον,
βλέπε, ὅτι οὗτος ἔσφα κται, καὶ τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ ῥεῖ, ὃ ἐκζητεῖ Θεός. Ἀπ ώλετο γὰρ ἡ
ζωτικὴ δύναμις αὐτοῦ· ἐκζητεῖ δὲ αὐτὸ ἀπὸ ἀδελφοῦ καὶ ἀπὸ θηρίου· ἀπὸ πιστοῦ
σκαν δαλίζοντος, καὶ ἀπὸ ἀλλοτρίου τῆς πίστεως, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ σκοποῦ.
Ἀλλὰ ταῦτα μὲν ἴσως περιεργότερον εἴρηται. Ὁ μέντοι ψάλλων διαλευκαίνει πᾶν τὸ
ἤδη ῥηθὲν, τό· Κατανοεῖ ὁ ἁμαρτωλὸς τὸν δίκαιον, φημί. Καθά περ γὰρ ἐν πίνακι
σαφῶς μηνιῶντα ζωγραφεῖ, καὶ παραταττόμενον εἰσφέρει, καὶ φονῶντα δεικνύει,
καὶ ἀπογυμνοῦντα τὸ ξίφος, καὶ ἤδη τοξεύοντα, καὶ τὴν ἀδικίαν αὐτοῦ καθίστησιν
ἐναργῆ. Σκοποὶ γὰρ τῷ ἁμαρτωλῷ οὐχ ἕνα τινὰ τῶν ἀδικησάντων αὐτῷ, ἢ κατά τι
προσκεκρουκότων, καὶ προφάσεις τῷ πολέμῳ δεδωκότων εὐλόγους ἀμύνεσθαι· ἀλλ'
ἵνα καταβάλῃ πτωχὸν, τουτέστι τὸν ἐπιεικῆ καὶ μετριόφρονα, καὶ ταπεινὸν τῇ
καρδίᾳ, ὃν καὶ ὁ Σωτὴρ πτωχὸν ἔφη τῷ πνεύματι, καὶ τῆς τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλείας
ἄξιον εἶναί φησι. Τίς οὖν τοῖς ἁμαρτωλοῖς λόγος πρὸς τοὺς εὐ θεῖς τῇ καρδίᾳ, καὶ
τοὺς πτωχοὺς τῷ πνεύματι; παντελῶς οὐδείς. Ἠδικήκασι γὰρ ἐκείνους οὐδὲν τὰς
ἑαυτῶν ὁδοὺς ἀπευθύνοντας εἰς δικαιοσύνην. Ἀκονᾷ δὲ, οἶμαι, κατ' αὐτῶν τοὺς
ὠνομασμένους, μάταιός τις ἁπλῶς, καὶ οὐκ εὐάφορμος φθόνος, ἐκ διαβολικῆς
σκαιότητος ἐκκεκαυμένος ἐν αὐτοῖς. Στίχ. ιεʹ. Ἡ ῥομφαία αὐτῶν εἰσέλθοι εἰς τὰς καρ
δίας αὐτῶν· καὶ τὰ τόξα αὐτῶν συντριβείη. Ὥσπερ δὲ ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ δικαίου εἰς αὐτὸν
ἀνακάμ πτει· οὕτως ἡ ῥομφαία τοῦ ἀσεβοῦς εἰσέλθοι εἰς καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, ἐὰν τηρῇ
ἑαυτὸν ὁ εὐθὺς τῇ καρ δίᾳ. Στίχ. ι ʹ. Κρεῖσσον ὀλίγον τῷ δικαίῳ ὑπὲρ πλοῦ τον
ἁμαρτωλῶν πολύν. Ἔχει μὲν οὖν ἡ λέξις αὐτόθεν ὠφέλιμόν τι τοῖς ἀκεραιοτέροις·
ἔχει δέ τι καὶ κεκρυμμένως εἰρημέ νον τοῖς βαθύτερον ἀκούειν τῆς Γραφῆς ἐπισταμέ
νοις. Τὸ οὖν ἁπλούστερον τοιοῦτόν ἐστι· Βιοπορι στοῦσι δίκαιοι καὶ ἄδικοι. Ἀλλ' οἱ
μὲν τοσοῦτον ζη τοῦσι τὸ τῆς χρείας, ὅσον τὸ τῆς δικαιοσύνης· καὶ ἢ οὐ πορίζουσιν, ἢ
ἄνευ ἀδικίας, χρωννύντες τὸ πορι ζόμενον τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ. Οἱ δὲ ὅλως νενεύκασιν
ἐπὶ τὸν πορισμὸν, ὅπως πολλὰ κτήσωσιν, οὐ ζητοῦντες εἰ καλῶς κτήσονται. ∆ύο οὖν
προκειμένων, τοῦ τε ὀλί 17.132 γου λήμματος μετὰ δικαιοσύνης, καὶ τοῦ πολλοῦ
μετὰ ἀδικίας· Κρεῖσσον ὀλίγον τῷ δικαίῳ ὑπὲρ πλοῦτον ἁμαρτωλῶν πολύν. Ἴδωμεν
δὲ καὶ τὸ ἀνακεχωρηκός. Κρεῖσσόν ἐστι πιστὸν ἰδιώτην εἶναι, οὐδὲ ἀνοῖξαι τὸ στόμα
δυνάμενον, ἢ πλουτεῖν τῷ λόγῳ προφορικῷ καὶ τοῖς μαθήμασιν ἐν κακίᾳ ἢ ἀπιστίᾳ.
Στίχ. ιζʹ. Ὅτι βραχίονες ἁμαρτωλῶν συντριβή σονται· ὑποστηρίζει δὲ τοὺς δικαίους ὁ
Κύ ριος. Ἐὰν ἴδῃς τὸν τόνον καὶ τὴν δύναμιν συντετριμμέ νην τοῦ ἀσεβοῦς, ὥστε μὴ
δύνασθαι αὐτὸν ἐκτεῖναι τὴν χεῖρα ἐπὶ πρᾶξιν ἀγαθὴν (συντετριμμένη γάρ ἐστιν),
ὄψει, ὅτι πεπλήρωται τό· Βραχίονες ἁμαρ τωλῶν συντριβήσονται. Ὁ δὲ συντρίβων, ὁ
διάβο λός ἐστι. Πᾶς μέντοι ἄνθρωπος ἀσθενὴς, καὶ τὸ ὅσον ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ καταπίπτει,
καὶ δέεται τοῦ ὑποστη ρίζοντος τοὺς καταπίπτοντας, καὶ ἀνορθοῦντος τοὺς
κατεῤῥαγμένους. Στίχ. καʹ. ∆ανείζεται ὁ ἁμαρτωλὸς, καὶ οὐκ ἀποτί σει· ὁ δὲ δίκαιος
οἰκτείρει καὶ δίδωσιν. Ὑψηλότερον δέ· Ὅταν διδάσκῃ Παῦλος, ἤ τις ἕτε ρος τῶν
ἱερῶν μυσταγωγῶν, οἱ ἀκροαταὶ δανείζον ται τὸ δόκιμον ἀργύριον τῷ στόματι
Παύλου. Καὶ ὁ μὲν δίκαιος ἀποδίδωσι τοὺς τόκους, καὶ λέγει· Μνᾶν μοι ἔδωκας, ἰδοὺ
δέκα μνᾶς ἐποίησα. Πέντε τά λαντα ἔδωκας, ἰδοὺ ἔχω δέκα. Ὁ δὲ ἁμαρτωλὸς
ἀναλίσκει πάντα. Οὐκ ἔξεστι δανείζειν τὰ ἑαυτοῦ, ἤτοι διδάσκειν ὡς οἱ αἱρετικοί·
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless the Savior a chosen dart, and in accordance with the Savior the darts of God the holy ones piercing with a chosen dart, so that the one pierced I say: Pierced of love I am; thus the Antichrist a dart of the evil one. And all sinners darts of the devil, to whom 17.129 he makes use against the righteous. Behold a woman, and they counseled for you. If not a dart is burning, having fire in mouth, that he may speak and burn you, in hand, in the whole body, in the whole soul; and as God places a bow in the cloud, that he may cease the storm, and not happen a flood; so, according to the opposite, the evil one makes use of a bow, that he may cease calm from the soul, and peace extinguish, and war raise, and storm make. Lest perhaps the poor and needy brothers are of the upright in heart, the poor in spirit, whom the demons seek to cast down. If you see one scandalized, and held under sin, behold, that he has been slain, and his blood flows, which God seeks. For his vital power has perished; and he seeks it from a brother and from a beast, from a faithful slanderer, and from alien of the faith, and from the hand of the aim. But these things perhaps have been said too subtly. The meanwhile the one singing makes white all that has been said, to wit: The sinner observes the righteous, I say. For as in a tablet clearly indicating one depicting, and bringing forward alongside, and showing one slaying, and exposing the sword, and already shooting, and establishing his injustice evident. For aims to the sinner not one of those having wronged him, or according to things having conspired against him, and pretexts having given to the war benevolent to defend themselves; but In order that he may cast down a poor person, that is, the gentle and moderate-minded person, and humble in heart, whom also the Savior called poor in spirit, and says he is worthy of the kingdom of the heavens. What then is the word to the sinners against the upright in heart, and the poor in spirit? Absolutely none. For they have wronged those [people] not even by their own ways being directed toward righteousness. But I think it happens also against them, the so-called [ones], some empty person, and not a gentle envy, inflamed from diabolical wickedness in them. Verse 15. Let their sword enter into their hearts; and let their bows be broken. Just as the peace of the just returns into him, so let the sword of the impious enter into his heart, if the upright one guards himself in heart. Verse 16. Better is little to the just than the abundance of the wicked. Indeed the word itself has something useful from the outset for the more innocent; and it has something also secretly said for those who understand to listen more deeply to the Scripture. Therefore the simple thing is this: The rich and the poor stand together, just and unjust. But the former seek only as much as the need, equal to the righteousness; either they do not obtain [it], or they obtain the thing to be acquired without injustice, pursuing the acquisition by righteousness. The latter have wholly turned toward acquisition, how they may gain many possessions, not seeking whether they will acquire well. Therefore two things are set before us: the little amount with righteousness, and the much amount with injustice. Better is little to the just than the abundance of the wicked. Let us also consider the withdrawn [thing]. Better is it to be a faithful private person, not even able to open the mouth, than to be rich in word spoken and in learnings in wickedness or unbelief. For the arms of the sinners shall be broken; but the Lord upholds the righteous. If you see the tension and the strength broken of the wicked one, so that he is not able to stretch out his hand to good action (for it is broken), you will see that it is fulfilled: The arms of the sinners shall be broken. And the one breaking, the devil, is he. But every man is weak, and as much as depends on himself falls down, and he needs the one upholding the fallen, and setting upright the broken.
pass_b_english: Nevertheless the Savior is a chosen dart, and the holy ones pierce with a chosen dart in accordance with the Savior, just as the darts of God correspond to Him; thus I say of the one who is pierced: I am pierced by love; and so the Antichrist is a dart of the evil one, and all sinners are darts of the devil, whom he uses against the righteous as referenced in 17.129. Behold a woman, and they counseled for you. If the dart is not burning, yet it holds fire in the mouth so that it may speak and burn you—in hand, in the whole body, in the whole soul—just as God places a bow in the cloud to cease the storm and prevent a flood, so too, in opposition, the evil one uses a bow to dispel calm from the soul, extinguish peace, raise war, and stir up storm. Perhaps the poor and needy are brothers who are upright in heart, poor in spirit, whom the demons seek to cast down. If you see one scandalized and held under sin, behold that he has been slain and his blood flows, which God seeks; for his vital power has perished, and he seeks it from a brother, from a beast, from a faithful slanderer, from one alien to the faith, and from the hand of the aim. But these things may have been said too subtly. Meanwhile, the one who sings makes clear all that has been said, namely: The sinner observes the righteous, I say. For just as on a tablet one clearly depicting is shown, brought forward alongside, one slaying is exposed, the sword is laid bare, already shooting, and his injustice is made evident. For the aims of the sinner are not directed at those who have wronged him, nor at those who have conspired against him, nor at those who have given benevolent pretexts for war to defend themselves; but

the focus shifts to the inner transformation wrought by song, which illuminates the prior declarations, revealing the sinner’s perception of the righteous not as accusation but as invitation to witness, where the act of singing does not erase the preceding imagery of conflict and judgment but rather refracts it through a lens of clarity, making manifest what was implicit: that the sinner’s gaze upon the righteous is not borne of hostility but of a dawning awareness, a recognition that persists even amid the surrounding metaphors of darts, bows, blood, and spiritual warfare, where the sacred and the profane intertwine in the human soul’s struggle, and the singer’s voice becomes the medium through which the hidden symmetry between sin and righteousness is disclosed—not as contradiction, but as fulfillment in tension.
The purpose is to bring low the poor person, meaning the gentle, moderate-minded, and humble in heart, whom the Savior also called poor in spirit and declared worthy of the kingdom of heaven.
What word is there for sinners against the upright in heart and the poor in spirit? None at all.
For they have wronged those people not even by directing their own ways toward righteousness.
I think it also occurs against them, the so-called ones: some empty person, not a gentle envy, but one inflamed from diabolical wickedness within them.
Let their sword enter their hearts; let their bows be broken.
Just as the peace of the just returns to him, so let the sword of the impious enter his heart, if the upright one guards himself in heart.
Better is a little for the just than the abundance of the wicked.
Indeed, the word itself has something useful from the outset for the more innocent, and it also contains something secretly said for those who understand to listen more deeply to Scripture.
Therefore the simple thing is this: the rich and the poor stand together, both just and unjust.

But the former seek only as much as the need, equal to righteousness; either they do not obtain it, or they obtain what is to be acquired without injustice, pursuing acquisition through righteousness.
The latter have wholly turned toward acquisition, seeking to gain many possessions, not considering whether they will acquire well.
Thus two things are set before us: a little amount with righteousness, and a much amount with injustice.
Better is little for the just than the abundance of the wicked.
Let us also consider the withdrawn thing: better is it to be a faithful private person, unable even to open the mouth, than to be rich in spoken word and in learning through wickedness or unbelief.
The arms of sinners will be broken, but the Lord supports the righteous.

When you observe that the strength and power of the wicked have been shattered—so much so that they cannot extend their hand to perform a good deed, since their strength is indeed broken—you will recognize that the prophecy has been fulfilled: the arms of sinners are broken.
The one who breaks them is the devil.
Nevertheless, every human being is weak, and whatever relies solely on oneself collapses; thus, each person requires the one who sustains the fallen and raises up the broken.
